To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the data gathered at the quick clay landslide site was of a very high quality, that a multi disciplinary approach was necessary in order to gain the maximum information from the data and that the data was very useful in assessing the risks posed by the landslide and the potential for future landslides in the area.
A multi-disciplinary approach to quick clay landslide investigations is essential.

the data collected at the site is complex, that it is important to combine geophysical, geomorphic and geotechnical data in order to understand quick clay landslids and that the data collected can be useful in the assessment of risk and the development of remedial strategies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the nature of the geophysical and geotectonic data obtained at Esp, Trøndelag, Norway and the relationship of that data to the geotechnical data obtained from the site.
developing an understanding of the geology, geotechnical properties, and geophysical properties of the landslide area.
developing an understanding of the complex ground conditions in the Esp area and in particular the nature of the quick clay layers and the potential for quick clay landsliding in the area.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quick clay landslide which occurred in 2012 at Esp, Tröndelag, Norway was triggered by a combination of a large storm event, a period of high rainfall, and an area of high water table.
the area is underlain by a complex sequence of soft sensitive marine clays which have been subject to a number of past landslides, some recent, some more distant in the past.
the landslide at Esp is a typical example of a Norwegian marine clay quick clay landslide and that the area is now safe for habitation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of FHEM data, in particular, is a very useful tool for the rapid assessment of quick clay areas.

a combination of FHEM, LiDAR, ERT and RCPTU can be used to give a good overview of the area and to delineate the landslide and potential landslide areas, and to provide an indication of the depth and form of the landslide and run out.

FHEM and ERT are useful for overview mapping of the quick clay areas, LiDAR data for understanding the landslide trigger mechanisms and geotechnical data is useful for understanding the geology and the nature of any quick clay deposits.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of geophysical methods in conjunction with geomorphological and laboratory investigations can be very powerful and that such an approach can be used to provide a good overview of the ground conditions and to provide the data necessary to assess the risk of quick clay landsliding in a given area.
it is possible to combine geophysical, geomorphic and geotechnical techniques to provide a comprehensive understanding of the hazard posed by a quick clay landslide.
a multi disciplinary approach is required to fully understand and map quick clay landslide hazards.
